newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crudes becalmed ahead of August liftings.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crudes becalmed ahead of August liftings.

text.p: Outright Brent values weakened on Wednesday but physical North Sea crude was inactive, becalmed in a lull in loadings between the end of July and start of August programmes, traders said.
Buying interest for the handful of July cargoes still available was sporadic but traders said the few substantive discussions that took place saw aggressive bidding.
"There is a lack of energy from buyers, they are staying very low profile," said one trader.
One European major held two Forties and one Statfjord loading in July.
Another major is seeking to move three Brents.
"We'd short anything close to 40," a trader said, referring to the 40 cent premium to Dated done last week for Forties.
Outright prices were showing gentle pressure. Front month August was down one cent at $18.38 a barrel after a steep rise on Tuesday on the back of bullish gasoline demand and U.S. stock data.

Traders said that while the front end of the market was looking relatively stable, second decade August dates and loadings further out were vulnerable to any further progress in efforts to resume Iraqi exports.

They noted comments from diplomats in New York on Tuesday that implied that Iraq will have to sell oil at a much higher rate in August than was previously thought in order to sell a billion dollars' worth by the 90 day deadline.
The U.N. resolution allowing the oil sales came into effect on June 8.
Paper markets were mostly talked firmer but mainly inactive, with traders avoiding potential volatility involved in the expiry of the August contract.
Intermonths were steady. Brent Aug/Sep was done at -5 and -4 cents, after -7, -5 and -4.5 cents were done on Tuesday.
Sep/Oct was done twice at -9 cents.
Brent CFDs for next week were talked five cents stronger at September Brent -16/-13 cents. The following week (July 28-August 1) was discussed three cents firmer at September -18/-14 cents.
